steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Equality Act 2010 consolidated and simplified previous anti-discrimination legislation into a single Act, replacing the Race Relations Act, Sex Discrimination Act and Disability Discrimination Act among others

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Act protects nine protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Direct discrimination occurs when a person is treated less favourably because of a protected characteristic (e.g. refusing a job to someone because of their race)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Indirect discrimination occurs when a provision, criterion or practice is applied to everyone but puts people with a protected characteristic at a particular disadvantage and cannot be justified as a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: List the nine protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010. | Q: What is the difference between direct and indirect discrimination? | Q: What is the duty to make reasonable adjustments and who does it apply to?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the specific protected characteristic when discussing a discrimination scenario — do not just say 'discrimination' Distinguish clearly between direct and indirect discrimination — use definitions and examples for both When discussing disability, always mention the duty to make reasonable adjustments — it is a unique feature of disability discrimination Remember that indirect discrimination can be justified but direct discrimination (except for age) generally cannot Use the correct legal terminology: 'protected characteristic', 'provision, criterion or practice', 'less favourable treatment' — not colloquial terms
